title: AgenTuna store layout and initialization
description: at-store owns the canonical store for four scopes: Global resolved through TF-022 AppPaths, User at ~/.agentuna, Project at ./.agentuna and Local at ./.agentuna/local for the active project. Layout: skills/<slug>/SKILL.md plus bundled assets, rules/AGENTS.md, mcp.json, store.json manifest, backups/, .state/ for journals, locks, staging and tmp, and local/ as Local scope content (project store only; the User store has no local/). init_store(scope, root) is idempotent and never clears an existing directory: it creates only missing entries with mode 0700 and writes schema_version:1 store.json when absent. A store.json with an unknown schema aborts with StoreError::UnknownSchema. A chosen root containing foreign files is accepted with a warning and the foreign paths are listed, never touched. Project stores are created on demand when a repo is added and the resolved path is persisted in projects. Global scope is read-only unless the process can write the admin path; failures surface as a permission error, not a silent fallback.
acceptance: init_store on an empty temp HOME creates skills/, rules/, mcp.json, store.json, backups/ and .state/; a second call changes no bytes and returns the same store_id, and a Project store additionally creates local/
A root containing foreign files is accepted, foreign paths are reported, and no foreign file is deleted, moved or rewritten
store.json with schema_version:99 returns StoreError::UnknownSchema and the caller renders the newer-version message
Skill slugs are validated as lowercase, separator-free, not dot-prefixed; a colliding slug is stored as name-2 and both items keep distinct ids
The Global root equals TF-022 AppPaths.global_store, including the AGENTUNA_GLOBAL_STORE override
notes: Global path comes only from TF-022 AppPaths; project path persisted in projects.

title: Store manifest schema, item ids and content hashes
description: store.json is the only item manifest: {schema_version:1, store_id: uuidv7, scope, updated_at, items:[...], disabled:[...]}. Each item record carries the decision-3 keys id, kind, slug, path and hash plus optional name and source metadata; the ItemId comes from TF-002 (itm_ + UUIDv7, allocated once, never reused). disabled is the per-scope disable tombstone list: [{item_id, kind, agents: [agent_id,...] | null}], where agents null means every agent. Entries are validated to reference an existing item_id of the same kind, an agents list is non-empty and duplicate-free, and tombstones commit atomically with the manifest; TA-003, TM-004 and TS-011 read and write this key but TC-002 owns its schema and validation. mcp.json is content only: {schema_version:1, servers:{<slug>: def}}, never a second item manifest and never carrying item ids. Hash contract: a skill uses a tree hash, sha256 over sorted lines of rel_path, size and sha256(bytes) for every file, so mtime does not matter; an MCP entry uses sha256 over canonical JSON with sorted keys, no insignificant whitespace and ${VAR} references kept literal; a rule uses sha256 over CRLF-to-LF normalized bytes. Manifest serialization is deterministic: items sorted by kind then slug, fixed key order, trailing newline, atomic temp-file rename. ItemId allocation and retirement stay with TF-002; store.json persists ids and never re-issues one.
acceptance: Copying a skill folder or touching mtimes leaves its hash unchanged; editing one byte of SKILL.md changes it
Reordering frontmatter keys and changing CRLF to LF leaves the rule and MCP hashes unchanged, while changing an env value changes the MCP hash
Two saves of an unchanged store produce byte-identical store.json; concurrent readers never observe a partial manifest
Ids survive rename and scope move, a deleted id is not reused, and store.json remains the only item manifest (mcp.json has no item ids)

A disabled entry with a missing item_id, mismatched kind, empty agents list or duplicate item_id rejects the save with a field error; a valid tombstone survives load/save and agents null disables every agent
notes: Decision 16: TC-002 owns the disabled tombstone schema and validation.

title: Store load/save, locking, orphan and missing-file reconciliation
description: load_store takes a shared fs4 lock on .state/store.lock, reads store.json, hashes every listed path and returns StoreSnapshot with items classified Present, Modified (hash differs from manifest), Missing and Orphan (file under skills/ or rules/ absent from the manifest). mcp.json is reconciled too: server entries missing from the manifest are Orphan, manifest servers missing from mcp.json are Missing, and a changed server definition is Modified. save_store requires the manifest hash observed by the caller and fails with ConcurrentModification when another process or editor changed store.json in the meantime. reconcile(snapshot, mode) either reports only (default) or imports orphans and drops missing entries after an explicit confirmation token; it never deletes orphan files from disk. The store keeps a temp staging directory under .state/staging/ and renames into place. read-only mode is used by CLI status and by the Global store when not writable.
acceptance: A second process writing store.json between load and save causes save_store to return ConcurrentModification and the first process's changes are not applied
An unknown skill folder placed under skills/ appears as Orphan and reconcile in report mode leaves it byte-identical
A manifest entry whose folder disappeared is reported Missing and stays in the manifest until confirmed removal
Exclusive lock contention blocks the second writer and returns a lock-timeout error after 5 seconds instead of writing
An mcp.json server added or removed outside AgenTuna appears as Orphan or Missing, and reconcile in report mode leaves mcp.json byte-identical

title: Project store git contract: committed files versus ignored backups and local state
description: The Project store is a git-visible directory. at-store writes .agentuna/.gitignore containing .state/, local/, backups/, *.tmp, .DS_Store and any per-machine override file. Committed set: store.json, skills/, rules/, mcp.json, .gitignore; local/ holds real Local-scope content and is intentionally gitignored, while .state/ and backups/ are machine-local. The app detects whether the project store has uncommitted changes by shelling out to git and offers stage-in-git at the end of migration or add-skill, but never commits automatically and never runs git add -f. Before staging it verifies with git check-ignore that no backup or local file would be added, and warns when .agentuna is itself ignored by a parent .gitignore or nested in another repository. A project store that is a symlink or lives outside the repo root is rejected with a clear path error. Backups stay local per machine; remote backup covers the User store.
acceptance: .agentuna/.gitignore ignores .state/, local/ and backups/; git status after a migration lists only store.json, skills/, rules/, mcp.json and .gitignore
Stage-in-git never stages an ignored file and reports the exact paths it staged; with no git repo it returns NotAGitRepository without writing
A parent .gitignore rule that excludes .agentuna produces a warning naming the rule source
A symlinked .agentuna path is rejected before any store write
notes: Git interaction is limited to status/check-ignore/add; commits remain the user's action.

title: Store integrity check and manifest rebuild
description: verify_store recomputes every hash, detects duplicate names within a scope, files outside any item, symlinks that escape the store root and item directories with a missing SKILL.md. rebuild_manifest reconstructs store.json from disk when it is lost or corrupt: skills from skills/*/SKILL.md, rules from rules/*.md, MCP entries from mcp.json. Rebuild preserves ids for entries that match an existing recoverable id by (kind, name, content_hash), allocates new ids otherwise, and reports every decision. Rebuild never modifies item content, never touches agent folders and writes a pre-rebuild copy of the old manifest under backups/ when readable. Exit report counts added, matched, renamed and skipped entries.
acceptance: Deleting store.json and running rebuild yields a schema_version:1 manifest whose hashes match the on-disk items and is loadable by load_store
A corrupt manifest is copied to backups/ before rebuild and the corrupt bytes remain recoverable
Duplicate skill names are reported with both paths and rebuild picks the lexicographically first, leaving the other as Orphan
Rebuild of an unchanged store preserves existing item ids

title: Native item scanner across all adapters
description: Native skill discovery is the TS-026 capability; at-migrate::scan orchestrates it through the TA-020 AgentAdapter registry for claude_code, codex, omp, cursor and custom agents. at-migrate adds MCP and rule discovery: MCP sources include ~/.claude.json mcpServers, .mcp.json, ~/.codex/config.toml [mcp_servers.*] and ~/.omp/agent/mcp.json; rule sources include CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.local.md. Each result records kind, name, agent_id, source path, scope (home paths User, repo paths Project, *.local.* Local), content hash, parse status and whether the path is a symlink into an AgenTuna store. Items are matched to store items by (kind, normalized name): equal hash is Managed, different hash is Conflict (handed to TC-007), unmatched is NotInAgenTuna. The same physical file reachable through overlapping roots is reported once with all agents. A missing agent root is skipped with reason; an unreadable file yields a per-item error and the scan continues.
acceptance: Scan on a fake HOME finds a skill in ~/.claude/skills, a server in ~/.codex/config.toml and a rule in a repo AGENTS.md, each with the correct scope and agent
A skill folder reachable through two overlapping Codex roots appears once with both agent entries and one path
An unreadable skill folder yields ItemError with path and OS error while other items still return and the summary is marked partial
A symlink inside an agent folder pointing into the AgenTuna store is classified Managed and excluded from native rows
notes: TA-020 owns the AgentAdapter registry, TS-026 owns native skill discovery; no adapter path constants are duplicated in at-migrate.

title: Conflict detection with normalized content comparison
description: Conflict detection compares each scanned copy against the store copy and against other agents' copies. Normalization rules: SKILL.md frontmatter parsed with saphyr and compared with sorted keys and scalar values, body compared after CRLF-to-LF and trailing-newline normalization, bundled assets compared as a path-to-hash set; MCP entries compared as canonical JSON with sorted keys and ${VAR} references compared by name, not secret value; rule files compared after line-ending normalization. Output ConflictSet entries carry kind, name, copies A and B (agent, path, scope, raw hash, normalized hash), a unified diff produced with similar, and a proposed default resolution. Equal normalized hashes with different raw hashes are marked formatting-only and default to KeepA without a manual diff. KeepBoth naming generates candidates name-agent and name-2, validated against the store and all installed agent targets; an unresolvable collision blocks the resolution.
acceptance: Frontmatter key reordering, CRLF line endings and trailing spaces produce formatting-only, not a content conflict
An env value change in one Claude copy and a matching ${VAR} reference in the store copy is reported as a real conflict, and the diff never renders a secret value
KeepBoth returns two unique names validated against the store and every enabled agent's target directory
Two identical copies under different agents collapse to a single equal-hash group and no conflict row

title: Migration plan builder and dry run
description: build_plan(scan, resolutions, strategy) turns a scan plus per-conflict decisions into an ordered MigrationPlan persisted at .state/plans/<plan_id>.json. Resolutions are KeepA, KeepB or KeepBoth{names}. Strategy is ReplaceWithLinks or LeaveAndWatch. Steps are ordered BackupOriginal, CreateStoreItem, then WriteLink or WriteCopy (per agent copy-mode setting) or RecordWatched, plus RenderMcp for each affected agent config and RenderRule. The plan records counts of items, files created, files backed up, links written and files left in place, the per-step expected source and destination hashes, and a plan hash over the serialized steps. dry_run(plan) returns ordered rows {seq, action, src, dst, bytes, backup_path} and performs no write, no directory creation and no lock beyond a shared read lock. LeaveAndWatch creates no links, records deployments as Native/Watched and leaves originals byte-identical.
acceptance: Dry run on a populated fake HOME returns the exact ordered file list and leaves every mtime and byte unchanged
Plan counts equal the number of rows per action; an empty selection cannot produce an applicable plan
Editing any source file after planning changes its hash and invalidates the plan hash before apply
LeaveAndWatch plans zero WriteLink rows and records watched deployments for each migrated item

title: Migration apply as one backed-up operation with journal and rollback
description: apply_plan(plan_id) preflights the plan hash, every source hash, destination availability (free or AgenTuna-owned), store write access and free disk space, backs up every original into the TC-014 operation folder, then builds a ChangeSet of FileOps (TF-052 types) and hands it to the TF-053 journaled multi-file apply under the exclusive store lock. at-migrate adds migration-specific FileOps (create store item, replace original with link or copy, patch MCP and rule fragments), plan hashing and pre/post verification; TF-053 owns the journal under .state/, backup-before-mutation ordering and reverse-order rollback. Success records one operation of kind Migrate with operation_files rows and returns the operation id. Any failed step is rolled back by TF-053; an unfinished journal is resolved on next start to either the full pre-migration or full post-migration file set.
acceptance: Backups exist and are hash-verified in the TC-014 operation folder before the first original is moved; a backup failure aborts with no mutation
A failure injected at any step restores every original byte-identically (sha256 equal, mode preserved) and leaves no created link, copy or store item
After a crash at step N, restart yields either the full post-migration file set or the pre-migration file set, verified by a hash manifest of every touched path
A successful apply records one operation with every touched path and the exact pre and post hashes
notes: TF-053 owns journaling and rollback; this story adds migration preflight, plan hashing and migration-specific FileOps.

title: Generic operation undo for all operation kinds
description: undo_operation(op_id) works for every kind in the TF-009 enum, including Deploy, Undeploy, EditSkill, EditMcp, EditRule, Migrate, Adopt, Restore, Backup, Scan, Settings, Update, DriftAdopt, DriftRestore, SyncPush, SyncPull, RemoteBackup, RemoteRestore, Undo, Delete, Promote and Move. It restores from operation_files plus backups, refusing when a current disk hash differs from the recorded after_hash unless force (which first backs the current state up). The window is UNDO_WINDOW_DAYS from TF-023, fixed at 30 days. Migrate and Adopt operations additionally delete links and copies AgenTuna created and remove store items whose current hash still equals the recorded post-operation hash; other kinds restore their recorded files. Undo writes a new operation of kind Undo referencing the original via undo_of and creates its own backups. Expired, already-undone and unknown operations return typed errors, and backups stay unpruned while the operation is inside the window.
acceptance: Undo of an unchanged Migrate or Adopt operation restores every original to its pre-operation sha256 and removes the store items, links and copies it created
Undo of a DriftAdopt or SyncPush operation restores the recorded operation_files bytes and creates its own backup before writing
The window comes from TF-023 UNDO_WINDOW_DAYS (30): day 29 succeeds and day 31 returns UndoExpired, evaluated in UTC
A second undo of the same operation returns AlreadyUndone, and the first undo is itself undoable through the same API
notes: Decision 7: generic over every operation kind with migrate-specific link cleanup.

title: Single-item adopt
description: adopt_item(native_item) builds a one-item MigrationPlan from the scan record: verify the source hash still equals the scanned hash, check for a name collision in the store and enabled agents, choose a store slug, back up the source, create the store item, then by default replace the agent original with a link (copy when the agent is in copy mode) or keep it watched when the caller asks. MCP items adopt by copying the parsed server definition into the store mcp.json and rendering it back into the agent with a scoped patch; rules adopt by copying the file into rules/. The operation is undoable through TC-010. An unchanged ad-hoc file that vanishes between scan and adopt returns StaleScanRecord with the current path state.
acceptance: Adopting a scanned skill creates the store item, backs up the agent folder and leaves a symlink at the original path in link mode
An adopt after the file changed since scan returns StaleScanRecord and writes nothing
Adopting an MCP server patches only that server's JSON/TOML entry and leaves other servers and comments intact
The returned operation id is accepted by undo_operation and restores the pre-adopt tree

title: Drift detection from watcher events and hash comparison
description: DriftService subscribes to the TF-007 debounced watcher for installed agent paths, project stores and the User store. Each event is coalesced per path with a 500 ms debounce. Events matching a self-write registered by an in-flight or recently completed operation are dropped by the shared TA-081 suppression loop (same path plus expected post-write hash within its 5 s window). Otherwise the file is hashed and compared with item_versions.content_hash and the deployment expected hash, producing Drifted, LinkReplacedByFile (agent path was a symlink into the store and is now a regular file), LinkRemoved, FileDeleted or StoreFileEditedWhileLinked. Each event is written to drift_events with item_id, agent_id, scope, path, expected_hash, actual_hash, detected_at and resolved_at NULL for unresolved, and emitted to the UI bridge with its classification. Unreadable paths become Unreadable events (permission denied) instead of silent drops; missing agent roots are ignored. Bursts affecting many files under one skill coalesce into one event with a file count. No network access.
acceptance: An external edit to ~/.claude.json produces one unresolved drift event (resolved_at NULL) within 1.5 s naming the server and the changed hash
An AgenTuna write followed immediately by its watcher event produces no drift event
Replacing a skill symlink with a real edited folder yields LinkReplacedByFile with the link target recorded
A permission-denied agent path yields an Unreadable event that the UI shows, and other paths keep being watched
notes: Drift is owned by at-engine in the contract; at-migrate only supplies store/native knowledge.

title: Drift adopt and restore
description: adopt_drift(event_id) reads the on-disk version, verifies its hash still equals the event's actual_hash, backs up the current store copy, copies disk into the store (skill tree) or patches the agent config into the canonical store mcp.json/rules, updates item_versions and deployment hashes and closes the event. restore_drift(event_id) builds a diff of AgenTuna's last known version versus disk, re-hashes the disk file immediately before writing and aborts with DriftChangedAgain when it moved, backs up the disk file, then writes the store version atomically; for MCP it patches only the affected server entry via jsonc spans or toml_edit and never re-serializes the whole agent file. Both actions write an operations row and are undoable. A drift event whose item was deleted from the store returns OrphanedDrift and offers open-in-editor only.
acceptance: Adopt on-disk makes the store hash equal the on-disk hash, backs up the previous store version and closes the event
Restore AgenTuna version writes the last known version, backs up the disk file and preserves unrelated JSON/TOML comments and servers
A second external edit between diff and write returns DriftChangedAgain without writing
Either action produces an operations row accepted by undo_operation

title: Operation backup layout, catalogue and restore
description: Owns the operation backup layout: every pre-write copy goes to backups/<utc-ts>-<operation_id>/<scope>/<relpath> with a .json sidecar carrying original_path, content_hash, size, mode and operation_id, and a backups catalogue row using the content_hash column. Built on the TF-041 copy, hash verification and restore primitive; TF-004 writes into the operation folder supplied by the caller. list_backups filters by path prefix, date range and operation. restore_backup(backup_id, confirm) backs up the current target first, recreates parent directories, writes atomically with the original mode, verifies content_hash and records a restore operation; a target changed since the backup requires confirm and a diff. Pruning is not implemented here: TF-050 owns retention and pruning (decision 19); this story sets expires_at from backup_retention_days and never deletes backup blobs or catalogue rows.
acceptance: A migration creates one catalogue row per original with content_hash matching the file and a path under backups/<utc-ts>-<operation_id>/<scope>/<relpath>, plus a sidecar
Restore of a deleted file recreates directories and content byte-identically; restore over a changed file requires confirm and first backs up the new state
Listing backups exposes operation id, original path, date and size so the drift screen can link a file to the run that touched it
notes: TF-041 supplies copy and restore; TF-050 is the only pruning implementation (decision 19).

title: Project sync-label consumption and action mapping
description: Consumes SyncLabel from TA-005 for project-store items and never derives it. It asks TA-005 for each project item on load, project switch, store change and after push or pull, returns the label unchanged plus the evidence hashes TA-005 recorded, and maps the label to the allowed action: push for ProjectNewer and ProjectOnly, pull for LibraryNewer and LibraryOnly, compare for Conflict and Drifted, none for InSync. Caching is keyed by item id and invalidated by the TA-005 state version. No hash matrix or base-hash arithmetic lives in this story.
acceptance: The returned label is exactly the TA-005 value for every fixture; a test stub changes TA-005's result and TC-015 follows without local recomputation
Action mapping covers InSync, ProjectOnly, LibraryOnly, LibraryNewer, ProjectNewer, Conflict and Drifted
The cache invalidates when the TA-005 state version changes and after any push or pull
No hash comparison or base-hash arithmetic is implemented in the at-engine sync wiring (grep test)
notes: Decision 12: SyncLabel is computed only in TA-005; this story consumes it.

title: Project sync push and pull with conflict refusal
description: push(project_item) copies the project copy into the User library; pull(library_item) copies the library copy into the project store. Both build a diff preview, backup the target, write atomically and update synced_hash on success. The target must still match the recorded base hash; otherwise the operation returns TargetChanged and requires the caller to review a diff and pass force, which backs up the changed target first. Push of a project-only item creates the library item; pull of a library-only item creates the project item. Rename detection matches equal content hashes with different names and offers rename instead of duplicate. Deleting is never implied by sync: a missing side is reported, not propagated. Each successful direction writes an operations row.
acceptance: Push of an in-sync item is a no-op with a clear already-in-sync result and no write
Push and pull refuse with TargetChanged when the destination hash differs from base, and force backs up the destination before writing
Rename with identical content is offered as a rename and does not create a second item
A missing project folder is reported, not recreated or deleted, by pull

title: Remote backup push to a private GitHub repo with Keychain token
description: at-git and at-secrets implement remote backup: the user pastes a GitHub token once, the token is validated with a repo-scope check, stored in the macOS Keychain under service dev.agentuna.remote-backup and never written to settings, logs, git config or command arguments (use a credential helper or GIT_ASKPASS temp file). The user names a device (default hostname, editable) and selects or creates a private repo on explicit action. Backup stages a temp clone, writes the store snapshot under stores/<store_id>/ (skills/, rules/, mcp.json, store.json), commits with a message containing device name and UTC timestamp, and pushes the default branch. Non-fast-forward is handled by fetching and handing off to the merge in TC-018; force push is never used. Status is persisted in remote_backup_state (repo_url, branch, last_commit, last_push_at, status, error_kind) and the device name is a settings value; conflict count is derived by query. Offline or auth failure returns a typed status and no retry loop; network only on explicit user action.
acceptance: Saving a token stores it only in Keychain; store.json, settings rows, git remote config and logs contain no token value
Backup creates a commit containing the full snapshot and updates last_commit and last_push_at; a second backup with no changes makes no empty commit
A rejected token returns an auth error naming the cause without echoing the token
Offline returns status offline and leaves the previous last_commit untouched
notes: Keychain API is at-secrets; the TM slice owns its story ids.

title: Multi-machine library sync without overwriting local copies
description: sync_from_remote() fetches the backup repo to a temp directory and compares the remote snapshot with the local store and the base commit stored in remote_backup_state. Cases: remote-only item is added locally after a backup, with a name collision resolved to name-<device>; local-only item is retained and pushed; both sides changed since base produce no overwrite, instead the remote copy is written under .state/remote-conflicts/<device>/<timestamp>/ and the item is marked Conflict in the UI with both paths. Identical content merges silently. Deletions are not propagated automatically: a remote-deleted item that is locally unmodified is removed only after confirmation, otherwise it is kept. After merge the app commits and pushes a snapshot, updating last_commit and recording the device name in the commit trailer. Re-running sync with no changes is a no-op and produces no duplicate conflict folders. Conflict resolution uses TC-013-style diff and pick actions.
acceptance: Two devices editing the same skill differently result in two preserved copies plus a conflict entry; neither original is replaced
A remote-only skill is added locally and a local-only skill is pushed in the same run without data loss
A remote deletion of an unmodified item asks for confirmation; a locally modified deleted item is kept
Running sync twice with no changes performs no commit, no duplicate conflict folder and no file rewrite
notes: Repo layout uses the store snapshot from TC-017; conflict copies live under .state/remote-conflicts, covered by the .state/ ignore rule (TC-004).

title: Remote restore and offline behaviour
description: restore_from_remote(commit) supports a new machine or disaster recovery. It lists remote commits with device, timestamp and item count, previews the snapshot against the local store, and writes selected or all items only into an empty store unless the caller explicitly chooses merge, which defers to TC-018. Snapshot integrity is verified against the store.json hashes before any write; a corrupt or truncated snapshot aborts with a named failing item. Restore backs up any existing target, writes atomically, sets last_commit and creates an operation row. Partial download failures return a resumable error with one explicit retry action. When offline the screen shows the last known commit and a retry control; no background polling.
acceptance: Restore into a fresh profile reproduces every skill, rule and MCP entry with hashes equal to the snapshot
A snapshot with one corrupted skill fails before writing anything and names the item
Restore into a non-empty store refuses without merge confirmation
A dropped connection mid-download leaves the store unchanged and offers a single retry

title: Repositories over TF-014, TF-016 and TF-018 tables (no DDL)
description: at-db repositories and queries only; no CREATE or ALTER appears in this story (decision 8). Tables are owned by TF-014 (native_items, drift_events, locks), TF-016 (operations, operation_files, backups) and TF-018 (settings, secret_refs, remote_backup_state). Repositories: transactional replace_scan(scope) over native_items preserving first_seen_at and marking vanished rows missing; open and resolve drift over drift_events with resolution adopt, restore or ignore; insert and finish operations plus operation_files; backup queries by original_path, date range and operation; remote backup state read and write of the singleton row; settings reads for store paths and banner keys. native_items is rebuildable; operations, operation_files, backups, remote_backup_state and settings are not.
acceptance: No DDL in at-db changes: the story compiles against the TF-014, TF-016 and TF-018 schemas and a schema test asserts table names and columns are unchanged
replace_scan removes stale rows only for the scope, preserves first_seen_at and marks vanished paths status=missing
Resolving a drift event writes resolved_at and resolution, is idempotent, and returns unresolved events newest-first
Deleting the DB and re-scanning rebuilds native_items while operations, backups and remote state are reported unrecoverable
notes: Decision 8: DDL ownership is TF-only; this story supplies repositories and queries.

title: Migrate screen 1: Scan
description: ui/src/screens/migrate renders wizard step 1. Empty: scanned folders list with zero counts and a Rescan button. Loading: per-adapter progress with a cancel action; results stream in as Tauri events from app::bridge jobs. Error: adapter failure or permission-denied path shows a warning row naming the path while partial results remain usable. Populated: table of found items with kind, name, scope, found in (agent and path), state (In AgenTuna, Conflict, Not in AgenTuna), Symlink badge and checkbox; select all per group; summary counts; Next disabled until at least one item is selected. Rescan preserves selections by (kind, path, hash) and clears stale selections. Uses TU-003 table, TU-002 badges and toasts from TC-029.
acceptance: All four states render with the contract module and no network access occurs during scan
A partial scan shows found rows plus a warning for the unreadable root; Next remains available for the found rows
Selections survive a rescan when path and hash are unchanged and are dropped with a notice when the item changed
Scanned folders are listed even when they contain zero items

title: Migrate screen 2: Resolve conflicts
description: ui/src/screens/migrate step 2 renders one conflict card per (kind, name): header with type and name, two columns showing scope, agent, path and short hash, a side-by-side diff of copy A and copy B using TU-007, and a radio group Keep A, Keep B, Keep both. Keep both reveals two name fields with live validation against store and agent targets. Formatting-only conflicts are pre-marked equal-content with Keep A default and an explanatory note. Bulk actions apply A or B to all unresolved conflicts. State lives in the wizard model so Back and Next preserve choices; Next is disabled while any conflict is unresolved. Empty state when the scan found no conflicts.
acceptance: Every conflict renders both paths and a diff; no secret values appear in MCP diffs
Keep both with an invalid name blocks Next and shows the validation message
Bulk keep-A resolves all unresolved cards but does not overwrite cards the user already chose
Formatting-only conflicts show as equal content and default to Keep A without requiring a click

title: Migrate screen 3: Plan, strategy and dry run
description: ui/src/screens/migrate step 3 shows store locations for the selected scopes, two strategy radio cards (Replace with links; Leave originals and watch) with an explanatory line per agent copy-mode, and counts of items, files created, files backed up, links written and files left. A Dry run toggle fetches the ordered plan rows through the bridge and renders src to dst, action and bytes; dry run never mutates and shows its own loading and error states. Apply requires a confirmation modal naming the counts and the backup directory. Warnings render for Global-scope items, locked items and conflicts that were force-resolved. Errors from plan generation show the offending path and keep the user on the step.
acceptance: Choosing a strategy recomputes counts without writing any file
Dry run lists every planned path in execution order and its result matches the applied operation file list in tests
Apply is unavailable until the confirmation checkbox is ticked and shows the backup location
A plan-generation error names the path and keeps prior selections

title: Migrate screen 4: Done, undo and failure recovery
description: ui/src/screens/migrate final step shows the applied summary (items moved, files linked, files left, backup path), per-step results from the operation, and an Undo migration button with the expiry date computed from the 30-day window. Undo shows a confirmation, a progress state and either success plus a toast or an UndoBlocked list of changed paths with a force option. PartialFailure renders failed steps with cause, the rolled-back status and a Retry action; an unfinished journal renders Resume or Roll back. Success links to Skills and to the Backups list. Failure must never display success counts for steps that rolled back.
acceptance: Successful apply shows counts matching operation_files and an Undo button labelled with the expiry date
A rolled-back apply shows zero completed steps and no Undo button, with the failing step named
UndoBlocked lists each changed path and requires explicit force before proceeding
After 30 days the button is absent and the screen explains the window has closed

title: Native rows, not-in-AgenTuna banner and single-item adopt
description: ui/src/screens/skills and ui/src/screens/mcp_list render native items returned by the scan. Rows carry a Not in AgenTuna tag with agent and source path, a Conflicts tag when applicable, and an Adopt button. A banner above the table states N items in agent folders are not in AgenTuna with Review & migrate and Hide; Hide persists per kind in the settings key native_banner_hidden.<kind> (TF-023) and is restorable from Preferences (TU-019). Adopt opens a one-item confirmation listing what will be created, linked or backed up, then calls TC-011 and refreshes only the affected row on success. Conflict rows open migrate step 2 preselected. Locked and Global rows show read-only affordances with a tooltip. Zero native items renders no banner.
acceptance: The banner shows the exact native count and both actions work; Hide writes native_banner_hidden.<kind> and survives an app restart
Preferences exposes the same banner toggle and turning it back on restores the banner without a rescan
Adopt confirmation names the store target and backup directory before any write
After adopt the row becomes a managed row without a full rescan
A stale scan record shows the StaleScanRecord error and offers Rescan instead of retrying blindly
notes: Banner visibility is owned by this story; persistence is the TF-023 settings key.

title: Sync and drift screen with split diff and backups list
description: ui/src/screens/drift has two tabs. Drift tab: header with in-sync item count and a watching indicator (active, paused, error with path); drift rows with item, agent, path, change kind and detected time; selecting a row shows a split diff AgenTuna's last known versus on disk via TU-007 and buttons Adopt on-disk, Restore AgenTuna version and Open in editor. Restore and adopt open confirmations naming the backup first. Backups tab: table of backup rows with created time, original path, size, operation and Restore (diff plus confirm). States: empty Everything is in sync, loading, watcher error with manual Rescan, permission error row. A compact drift banner appears above Skills and MCP lists with a count linking here. No network.
acceptance: Drift rows render every detected kind including LinkReplacedByFile and Unreadable, and the split diff shows both versions
Adopt and Restore update the row and the in-sync count without a restart
Backups tab lists backups with dates and Restore works for a deleted file
Watcher error state shows the failing path and a working manual rescan

title: Project sync label chips and push/pull actions
description: Project-scope rows and the skill detail sync section render the SyncLabel from TC-015 as a chip: In sync, Project only, Library newer, Project newer, plus Conflict when both sides diverged. Each row offers the action valid for its label: push up for Project newer, pull down for Library newer, Pull to project for Project only, Push to library for Library only, and Compare for Conflict. The action opens a diff modal built on TU-007 with confirm, then runs TC-016 and updates the chip and the library count. In sync rows show no action. Errors (TargetChanged, missing side) render inline in the modal with a force option after review. Labels refresh on project switch and after any sync action.
acceptance: Each of the four labels plus Conflict renders the correct enabled action and no action for In sync
Push and pull confirmations show the diff and the destination backup before writing
TargetChanged renders in the modal and force re-diffs instead of silently overwriting
Chips recompute after project switch without a restart

title: Remote backup settings: device name, GitHub token, sync status and conflicts
description: ui/src/screens/settings gains a Remote backup section. Fields: device name defaulting to hostname with validation, repo selector with create-private-repo action, and a token entry that is masked, cleared after save and stored through at-secrets; the token is never displayed again, only a Connected as state. Status panel shows last backup time, last commit, conflict count and offline state with a single Retry. Actions: Backup now, Sync from remote, Restore from remote (opens commit list), Resolve conflicts (opens the conflict list with paths under .state/remote-conflicts and links to the drift-style diff). Destructive actions require confirmation naming the device and repo. All calls are explicit; no polling. Error states cover invalid token, missing repo, network offline and read-only repo.
acceptance: After saving, the token field is empty and no screen or log can reveal the token
Device name validation blocks slashes and empty values and is used in the commit trailer
Backup now, Sync and Restore show progress and final status without blocking the UI thread
A conflict list shows both copies and never offers a silent overwrite action

title: Migrate, drift and backup toast catalogue
description: Wire the O13 toast service (TU-005) for store and migration flows with exact copy and actions: adopt-first warning when toggling an unmanaged native item (Adopt action), migration complete (N items moved, Undo action), migration rolled back (error, persistent until dismissed), undo complete, undo blocked (Review changes action), drift detected per item (Review action, deduplicated per item within 10 s), restore from backup complete, remote backup complete and remote conflict found. Success and warning toasts auto-dismiss after 2.5 s; errors persist until dismissed and are also listed on the relevant screen. Toasts must not fire for self-write suppression or for scan refreshes, and repeated identical toasts replace rather than stack.
acceptance: Each listed event produces exactly one toast with the specified copy and action target
Self-write watcher events and rescans produce no drift toast
Repeated drift on one item within 10 s does not stack duplicates
Error toasts persist until dismissed and remain visible after navigating screens

title: agentuna migrate and adopt commands with JSON output
description: at-cli registers the migrate and adopt command groups on the TU-026 CLI tree (noun-first): migrate scan, migrate plan, migrate apply, migrate undo, migrate status and adopt, all using the same at-migrate engine as the GUI. Examples: agentuna migrate scan --json; migrate plan --strategy links|watch --dry-run --json; migrate apply --plan <id> --json; migrate undo <operation-id> [--force] --json; adopt <path> [--keep] --json. JSON uses the TU-033 envelope {ok, data|error:{code,message,details}, warnings}; typed codes (needs_resolution, stale_plan, undo_expired, partial_failure) are emitted as error.code and TU-033 exit codes apply. Non-interactive mode refuses to guess conflicts and requires --keep-a, --keep-b or --keep-both. Dry run writes no file. Human output renders tables with counts.
acceptance: migrate scan --json on a fake HOME emits one record per native item with kind, scope, path and state and exit 0
migrate apply --dry-run --json lists the exact file operations and creates no file, lock or journal
Ambiguous conflicts without a keep flag exit with the TU-033 needs-resolution code and write nothing
Undo after the 30-day window exits with the TU-033 user-error code, error.code undo_expired, and changes nothing

title: agentuna drift, backups, sync and remote commands
description: at-cli registers the drift, backups, sync and remote command groups on the TU-026 CLI tree (noun-first): drift list --json, drift adopt <event>, drift restore <event>, backups list --json, backups restore <id>, sync status --json, sync push <item>, sync pull <item>, remote status --json, remote backup and remote restore <commit>. Read-only commands never mutate state and never contact the network except remote status when --refresh is passed. Destructive commands require --yes in non-interactive use. Output uses the TU-033 envelope and exit codes; typed codes (drift_changed_again, target_changed, undo_expired, offline, auth_failed) are error.code values. The CLI shares the app database path and respects single-writer locking; it reports when the GUI holds the lock.
acceptance: drift list --json reports open events with item, path and hashes and performs no writes
sync status --json returns the label and evidence hashes for a project item
remote commands fail with auth_failed without echo of the token and without creating a repo when the token lacks scope
A destructive command without --yes exits with the TU-033 usage-error code and changes nothing

title: Migration link replacement, link rollback and junction fallback
description: Migration-specific link handling built on the TF-006 symlink/copy primitive and the TS-027 per-agent link policy. During apply, each original scheduled for replacement is backed up, then recreated at its agent path as a symlink on macOS/Linux or a directory junction on Windows pointing at the store; the plan records the link target so undo deletes the link and restores the original bytes. If link creation fails (EPERM, EXDEV, Windows without symlink privilege, network volume, symlink creation refused), that step falls back to copy mode for the item, records deployment mode=copy with a warning and continues; the fallback is journaled so rollback removes whichever artifact (link or copy) was created. Writes open targets no-follow so a symlinked agent path cannot redirect an AgenTuna write outside the intended tree. Case-insensitive name collisions (Foo versus foo) are rejected during planning. Permission denied on an agent folder yields an actionable error naming the path and required permission; macOS TCC-protected locations are named as such. Paths exceeding the platform limit are rejected during planning.
acceptance: On a filesystem that rejects symlinks, the migration step records copy mode and completes with a warning; no partial link remains
A case-insensitive collision between two scanned item names is reported before the plan runs
Undo and rollback remove the created link or copy and restore the original path byte-identically with no dangling link
A permission-denied agent folder produces a typed error naming the path and the migration rollback leaves originals intact
notes: Link primitive and copy fallback are TF-006; agent link policy is TS-027. This story covers only migration-specific replace, rollback and junction fallback.

title: Store layout, manifest and golden-file round-trip tests
description: Test suite using the TF-010 temp HOME fixture. Covers init idempotence, manifest deterministic serialization (byte golden), hash stability for skill trees, MCP canonical JSON and rule files, orphan and missing reconciliation, corrupt manifest rebuild, and store load/save under lock contention. Golden files for store.json, mcp.json and rules output live under test fixtures; an intentional formatting change must fail the golden so serialization drift is caught. Includes a rebuild test that deletes store.json and asserts equivalent content with preserved ids, and a cross-platform newline test.
acceptance: Golden comparisons for store.json and mcp.json pass on a clean run and fail when a key order or newline changes
Hash stability tests cover mtime change, folder copy, frontmatter reorder and CRLF conversion
Orphan, missing and corrupt-manifest cases assert exact classifications and that no orphan file is deleted
A second load/save cycle produces byte-identical output

title: Conflict normalization and migration plan matrix tests
description: Table-driven tests over the conflict normalizer and plan builder. Conflict fixtures: frontmatter key order, CRLF, trailing spaces, asset-only difference, MCP key order, equivalent ${VAR} refs, changed env value, and rule line endings; expected formatting-only versus conflict classifications. Plan fixtures: every strategy and resolution permutation, keep-both naming collisions, empty selection, mixed skill/MCP/rule items, and counts consistency. A dry-run versus apply equivalence test runs both against the same fixture and asserts the dry-run row set equals operation_files. Snapshot-style assertions keep diffs readable.
acceptance: Every normalization fixture produces the expected classification and diff presence
Keep-both name generation is tested for store collision, agent collision and both, with the exact chosen suffix
Plan counts equal row counts for every action across all strategy and resolution permutations
Dry-run rows equal the applied operation_files for the same fixture

title: Migration apply and undo integration tests
description: End-to-end tests on fake Claude, Codex, omp and Cursor homes plus a project store. Scenarios: migrate three skills, two MCP servers and one rule with replace-with-links; verify symlinks, store contents, backups and operations rows. Undo and verify every original is byte-identical by sha256 and mode, links and created store items are gone, and agent config files match their pre-migration bytes. Time-travel the clock to day 31 and assert UndoExpired. Assert double undo fails, undo of an adopt works, leave-and-watch leaves originals untouched and records watched deployments, and re-apply after undo produces an equivalent state. Included because undo is a load-bearing promise.
acceptance: Apply then undo restores every original byte-identically across all four agent fixtures
Undo at day 31 is refused with UndoExpired and day 29 succeeds
Double undo returns AlreadyUndone without touching files
LeaveAndWatch leaves every original hash unchanged and creates no link

title: Partial-failure rollback and crash-recovery tests
description: Fault-injection tests around apply_plan. Each journal step is failed in turn: backup copy error (disk full), symlink EPERM, store write error, MCP patch parse failure, rule write failure, and process abort after step N simulated by dropping the runtime and reloading the TF-053 journal. Assertions for every case: originals byte-identical to pre-migration, no dangling or duplicate links, store manifest equal to pre-migration, operation marked failed_rolled_back, backups retained, and a retry after fixing the fault succeeds. A crash case asserts the recovery prompt and both resume and rollback paths yield a consistent tree. Included because partial-failure rollback is a load-bearing promise.
acceptance: Failure injected at each step leaves every original hash unchanged and no created artifact behind
After a crash at step N, restart yields either the full post-migration file set or the pre-migration file set, verified by a hash manifest of every touched path
Rolled-back operations keep their backups and report the failing step and cause
Retry after removing the fault completes and produces a clean operation

title: Drift detection and sync label matrix tests
description: Watcher-driven integration tests with a fake HOME: external edit to a skill file, external edit to ~/.claude.json, linked folder replaced by a real folder, link deleted, store file edited while linked, permission-denied folder, and a burst of many files. Assert event kinds, hashes, debounce coalescing and timing under 2 s. Self-write suppression test runs an AgenTuna write and asserts no event. Sync tests feed each TA-005 label through TC-015 and assert the action mapping and cache invalidation; the derivation matrix itself is covered by TA-005's own tests. Also assert no network access during detection.
acceptance: Every drift kind is detected with the expected event fields and no false positive for self-writes
Link replacement is distinguished from a normal external edit
TC-015 passes through every TA-005 label unchanged and maps each to the expected action
Detection tests run offline and complete within the timing budget

title: Remote backup conflict, offline and restore tests
description: Tests against a local bare git repository acting as GitHub. Two device profiles with separate stores and device names. Cases: first backup creates the snapshot; remote-only item is added; local-only item is pushed; divergent edits preserve both copies and create a conflict entry with no overwrite; remote deletion of an unmodified item requires confirmation; local modification of a remote-deleted item keeps it; second sync is a no-op; restore into an empty store reproduces hashes; corrupt snapshot aborts. Token handling test uses a fake secret store and asserts the token never appears in committed files, logs or process arguments. Offline simulation returns offline without retries.
acceptance: Divergent devices never overwrite either copy and produce exactly one conflict record and two preserved files
Repeated sync with no changes makes no commit and no duplicate conflict folder
Restore reproduces every item hash; a corrupted snapshot aborts before any write
No test-visible artifact contains the fake token value
notes: Uses a local bare repo; no real GitHub calls in tests.

title: Concurrent external writer and lock-contention tests
description: Tests that a second writer cannot corrupt a migration or store write. Cases: external process modifies a source between plan and apply (hash mismatch aborts before backups); external process modifies a destination between preflight and write (at-fs optimistic concurrency recheck fails, rollback completes); external edit to store.json between load and save returns ConcurrentModification; two CLI processes contend on the fs4 store lock and the loser times out without writing; a same-content touch with mtime change is allowed because hash is unchanged; an external edit to an agent config during apply rolls back that step and leaves the agent file as the external writer left it. Runs with real child processes to avoid mocking the race.
acceptance: Every race case either applies a fully consistent change or aborts with the external writer's bytes intact
Store lock contention never produces a partial manifest write
A content-identical mtime change does not trigger a false concurrency failure
Agent files modified during apply are never overwritten by rollback

title: Drift adopt and restore tests
description: Integration tests for TC-013 on temp HOME fixtures. Scenarios: adopt on-disk after an external skill edit, adopt after an MCP config edit, restore AgenTuna over a changed skill, restore over a changed MCP server, restore after the item was deleted from the store, a second edit between diff and write, permission denied, and undo of each action through TC-010. Assertions: adopt updates the store hash and item_versions/deployment rows; both directions create a content_hash-verified backup before any write; restore preserves unrelated JSON/TOML entries and comments; DriftChangedAgain writes nothing; undo restores the exact pre-action bytes and removes links it created; no stale open drift_event remains after adopt or restore.
acceptance: Each adopt and restore scenario leaves the expected hashes in store, item_versions and deployments, with a matching backups row created before the write
Restore preserves unrelated MCP servers and TOML comments and never re-serializes the whole agent file
A second edit between diff and write returns DriftChangedAgain and changes no byte
Undo of drift adopt and drift restore returns the exact pre-action file set, including link removal for skills
notes: Destructive-path coverage for decision 12 drift adoption; complements TC-037 detection tests.
